comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text:
## Comparative test protocol added

The candidate branch now includes [ROBOT_LIGHTSHELL_COMPARATIVE_TEST_PLAN_V0_1.md](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/blob/research/robot-lightshell-atelier-v0-1-20261117/docs/research/ROBOT_LIGHTSHELL_COMPARATIVE_TEST_PLAN_V0_1.md).

The matched comparison is now explicit: bare robot, existing rigid/production cover, an ODD-matched commercial cover, textile-only, textile + 3D spacer, and textile + spacer + local guard. It separates coupon testing, kinematic fit, instrumented module comparison, motion/flex/cleaning, and lifecycle qualification. Hard safety/thermal/ROM/perception gates apply before Pareto ranking.

Industry research also supports two separate product archetypes: (1) conformal soft garment (domestic/service/research/selected industrial), and (2) sealed process cover (specific dust/liquid/chemical/food-process use). 1X NEO and ASP Protection are useful product-level comparators, but their published claims are not independent matched test results.

Exact pilot CAD, attachment interfaces, ODD, thermal/cable constraints and mass budget remain open. No physical article or material has been selected or tested.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text:
Added a machine-readable comparative benchmark manifest to draft [PR #12691](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/12691):

- `lightshell_benchmark.schema.json`
- `lightshell_benchmark.example.json`

The unrun seed fixture names six candidate architectures (B0–B2, L1–L3), seven initial metrics, and nine hard gates. Baselines remain unassessed, thresholds and baseline values are null, and every hard gate is unknown. This is deliberately an inputs-pending benchmark contract, not a result or qualification claim. Both JSON files parse, and a lightweight nested required-key/enum/constant check reported no errors.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text:
### New work added — sensor-ready textile research and executable evidence gate

- [LIGHTSHELL-SENSOR-FABRIC-001 #12704](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/12704) now owns removable tactile/strain/temperature sensing textiles. It compares 2026 fibre-piezoresistive and self-powered minimal-channel research with CushSense, requires wash/flex/humidity/calibration/fault testing, and explicitly keeps this layer observational—not safety-rated or motion-authorizing.
- Draft PR [#12691](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/12691) now includes a Rust qualification validator in `symthaea-engineering::lightshell_qualification`, plus a qualification contract and per-candidate benchmark manifest.
- The benchmark is no longer globally gated: it has 42 candidate-scoped metric rows and 54 candidate-scoped hard-gate rows (6 candidates × 7 metrics and 6 × 9 gates). It remains inputs-pending, with null measurements/thresholds and unknown gates.
- The validator only returns ranking-eligible candidates with a matched B0 baseline, same coverage boundary, passed per-candidate gates, an evidence-complete physical module/integrated test, no adverse run, and observed core metrics with method/uncertainty refs. It does not calculate a protection rating or authorize actuation.

Rust tests are authored but have not been executed in this environment. Exact-head CI status is read separately; skipped jobs are not passes. No CAD or physical qualification is claimed.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text: Further extension: [ROBOT-GARMENT-COMPILER-001 #12710](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/12710) is now open. It will take exact robot CAD, kinematics, swept link/cable envelopes and thermal/sensor/service keep-outs and generate *candidate* textile zones, panels, seams and manufacturing packages. The initial corpus is synthetic single-joint/elbow fixtures with unit/frame/seam/clearance negative controls. It composes #11731, #11750, Sol-Atlas #738 and Symtropy #456/#4865; it does not duplicate CAD or cloth solver owners.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text: The robot-garment compiler is no longer only a proposal. [ROBOT-GARMENT-COMPILER-001 #12710](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/12710) now has P0 implementation in [draft PR #12719](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/12719): synthetic elbow fixture + schema + Rust AABB geometry admission for panel-to-zone containment and clearance/uncertainty-expanded joint/cable/sensor/vent/service keep-outs. It is a conservative fit-screen gate, not mesh collision or physical safety qualification.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text:
### New material-science work opened

[LIGHTSHELL-SPACER-DOE-001 #12724](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/12724) applies the existing Atelier inverse-textile-design and experiment-selection stack to robot-zone spacer constructions. It adds a five-control comparison and a proposed 18-structure campaign (12 screening + 6 conditional transition refinements), with compression/impact, vibration, airflow, thermal, flex, cleaning and repair measured separately.

The January 2026 spacer-knit paper shows the relevant trade-off: in its tests, square-wave silicone inlays improved compression-energy absorption/force reduction, while some higher spacer-course frequencies improved vibration isolation but lowered impact-force absorption; the paper did not test washability/durability. The proposed DoE therefore avoids a universal best-fabric score and makes lifecycle a required response.

The schema, fixture and protocol plan are added to draft PR [#12691](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/12691). All samples remain proposed; no machine, yarn lot, material lot or process capability is assumed.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text: The spacer textile DoE now has a typed Rust admission module in draft [PR #12691](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/12691), alongside the Lightshell benchmark validator. It prevents confounded transition-spacing/frequency comparisons and requires the machine/process capability and preregistration evidence before the matrix can move into execution. Both modules have authored tests; neither has been compiled or executed yet.

comments.author: Tristan-Stoltz-ERC
comments.text: Follow-on engineering added: #12759 now includes ISO 25086-1:2026 snagging-method applicability; #12774 adds uncertainty-aware, process-bound robust zone candidate admission and interval-Pareto shortlisting. Both remain draft and software-only; this is not physical material or robot qualification. See the linked PRs for exact claim boundaries.
